Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming in iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful new capability: the ability to automatically change your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27, powered by Apple Intelligence, can handle compromised login accounts on your behalf.

The new generation of Apple Intelligence features is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One powerful new AI feature is related to Apple's Passwords app.

The Passwords app, launched two years ago, is a centralised hub dedicated to managing login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always alerted you to password issues in your database. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach, or if you've reused the same password across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

However, until now, you've still had to handle these problematic login accounts manually yourself.

But Apple says that in iOS 27, in many cases, a newly added intelligent agent AI feature can change your passwords on your behalf. According to its official website:

With this feature, you can keep your login accounts secure, always using strong passwords, without spending too much effort or time.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to roll out to all users in a few weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, but as the beta has been a bit rough, it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Feel free to share in the comments.
